objective: Assemble the transport-neutral Cloud IaC OpenTofu module registry HTTP handler into the repo-canonical Hyper-adapter Router<SyncHandler> plus middleware dispatch path without binding sockets, starting a listener, deploying an endpoint, or claiming FD-001 tenant workload hosting.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu clients discover service base URLs through /.well-known/terraform.json, including modules.v1.
The module registry protocol uses GET versions and download routes under the modules.v1 base; this slice only assembles dispatch for those route shapes.
Registry source strings identify reusable module packages; credentials, provider execution, OpenTofu plan/apply, and production serving remain separate concerns.

implemented_claims: Added oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter as an oya-cloud-iac-runtime dependency so module-registry handling can enter the canonical Hyper-adapter router/middleware dispatch path.
Added CloudIacModuleRegistryHttpServiceAssembly holding Router<SyncHandler>, MiddlewareChain<HttpRequest,HttpResponse>, and ServerConfig metadata.
Added assemble_module_registry_http_service to wrap CloudIacModuleRegistryHttpHandler with handler_to_sync and register the three OpenTofu module-registry GET route templates.
Added dispatch_module_registry_http_service_request to delegate request dispatch through oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter::dispatch.
Declared a service-assembly non-claim constant and max_body_bytes=0 metadata to distinguish local assembly from live server/listener/deployment evidence.
Updated Cloud IaC manifest, runtime catalog, tasks, multispectrum evidence, and audit chain for the service-assembly slice.
explicit_non_claims: no registry publish path or object-store serving
no request authentication or Cedar runtime integration beyond previously injected in-process authorization metadata checks
no module signing, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation generation
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD/Jenkins/GitOps integration beyond existing local evidence gates
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant workload evidence
false_green_findings_closed: Direct transport-neutral handler tests are not proof that the handler can be dispatched through the repo canonical router/middleware path; this slice adds focused tests that exercise oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter dispatch over registered OpenTofu routes.
Route registration counts and 404 behavior are asserted to prevent treating an unregistered or ad hoc handler call as service assembly evidence.
known_gaps: Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed by this ChangeSet; repo-wide unrelated blockers remain outside this Cloud IaC slice.

Cloud IaC still needs actual socket binding/listener, deployed live endpoints, registry publish path, object-store serving, auth runtime, database adapter, signing/SLSA/VSA, provider runtime, tofu test/plan/apply, and live GitOps/provider integration evidence.

FD-001 remains the master-plan product delivery goal; Oyatie Cloud must later prove substrate readiness by hosting FD-001 microservices as tenant workloads, but this ChangeSet provides no tenant-workload dogfood evidence.
Concurrent unrelated application-shell and other agent work exists in the worktree; this ChangeSet does not claim or modify those surfaces.
The complementary /Users/jasonlee/Developer/source/plan files informed sequencing only and are not treated as source-of-truth implementation evidence.

findings: The assembly is a thin composition seam: one Router<SyncHandler>, an empty MiddlewareChain, default ServerConfig metadata, and a dispatch wrapper. No ad hoc HTTP stack or duplicate route parser was introduced.

Moves Oyatie Cloud substrate toward a service-hostable internal module registry while preserving the boundary that live listener, deployed endpoint, provider runtime, and tenant workload claims remain false until later evidence exists.
FD-001 tenant workload dogfood hosting remains a future substrate proof, not a claim of this service-assembly slice.
RED test failed on missing assembly symbols before implementation; GREEN tests assert route registration count, max body metadata, adapter dispatch success, and unknown-route 404 behavior.
Future listener work can reuse assemble_module_registry_http_service rather than remembering three route templates or bypassing middleware/router dispatch.
Focused runtime tests, scoped Cloud IaC tests, fmt/check/clippy, architecture/api/planning gates, Cloud IaC regression gates, and aggregate run-all all passed.

findings: No credential, provider, tenant data, network bind, or persistence path was added. The assembly preserves existing handler authorization checks and sets max_body_bytes=0 metadata for GET-only routes.
Dispatch adds a single in-memory router/middleware hop over the existing handler. No blocking I/O, provider calls, filesystem reads, or OpenTofu invocation are added.
Manifest, catalog, tasks, evidence, and audit rows encode local-only service-assembly scope plus explicit nonclaims.
Registered route templates align with OpenTofu service discovery and module-registry protocol route shapes already enforced by Cloud IaC protocol fixtures.
Cloud IaC manifest, runtime catalog, tasks/plan, tasks/todo, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain entries were updated for traceability.
The service assembly exposes route_count, middleware_count, and server_config metadata for deterministic test/evidence inspection while avoiding live operations claims.
Oya VCS claim was used before source changes; no raw git/gh commands were used; architecture-boundaries role constraints remain green.
Official OpenTofu docs anchor route/protocol semantics, and repo-local evidence distinguishes local service assembly from live endpoint or production substrate readiness.
Explicit nonclaims exclude socket bind/listen/serve/deploy, auth runtime, persistence, provider execution, OpenTofu plan/apply, cloud provisioning, full verify, and FD-001 tenant hosting.
